text:
maya: Quick run posted comparing PCIe vs SXM across us-west/us-east with NVLink/NUMA pin configs. Short summary + config + numbers below. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/topo-smoke (internal). :chart_with_upwards_trend:

raj: nice. did you run with the new cuDNN kernel selection patch?

maya: yes, used KERNEL_SELECTOR=v2 (fallbacks enabled). command I used: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./run_infer_bench --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --profile`

bench-bot: automated note: benchmark run 1781249876 started by maya on gpu-cluster-uw1, 2 gpus, sxm nodes flagged as A100-SXM-80GB.

maya: TL;DR numbers (median/p95 latency single request, and steady-state tokens/s for continuous workload):
- PCIe (p4d-like, 8x40gb NVMe, no NVLink): p50=34ms, p95=145ms, tokens/s=4.8k (batch=8).
- SXM (NVLink enabled intra-node): p50=21ms, p95=68ms, tokens/s=7.1k (batch=8).
- SXM with NUMA pinning off (default scheduler): p50=26ms, p95=94ms, tokens/s=6.0k.

sasha: interesting p95 delta. so NUMA pinning recovered ~25% of p95 and ~18% tokens/s?

maya: right. NUMA pinning command I used for the SXM nodes: ```numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./run_infer_bench ...``` we bind worker threads to the CPU socket closest to the GPU PCIe root. when we didn't bind, context-switches to the other socket caused PCIe peer-to-peer fallbacks more often (even on NVLink fabrics) which increased tail latency.

oliver: are these runs using KV cache offload between GPUs? that matters a lot for multi-gpu attention.

maya: yes, KV is sharded across gpus (local KV kept on the gpu that started the request, remote fetch over NVLink/PCIe). I toggled two kernel paths: `CUTLASS_KERNEL` vs `CUSTOM_KV_PULL` (our optimized fused pull).

raj: kernel details? numbers per kernel?

maya: short: on SXM with NVLink the `CUSTOM_KV_PULL` gives ~10% higher throughput and ~12% lower p95 vs CUTLASS_KERNEL because we reduce memcpy and launch overheads. On PCIe the win is smaller (~4%) because PCIe bandwidth is the bottleneck.

bench-bot: note: quantization experiment attached: run 1781249902, int8 + config quant_profile=aggressive.

maya: quantization notes: int8 (GPT-like static QAT->PTQ pipeline) reduced memory footprint ~35% and improved tokens/s by ~20% on SXM, ~12% on PCIe. However eval on our regression suite showed generation-quality delta: 1.1% decrease in exact-match like metric, and 0.9 BLEU/ROUGE drop (small for many apps, unacceptable for some).

sasha: so for customers that care about deterministic quality we probably want int8 opt-in with eval guardrails. Can we gate rollback automatically on quality drift?

maya: yep, suggested rollout: canary int8 on non-critical routes + eval hooks; fallback to fp16 on regression detection. I added a draft canary policy in the run notes.

oliver: did you test cross-region (us-west -> eu) routing with fallback to smaller models? curious about latency when routing across regions vs local SXM pools.

maya: quick check: cross-region cold fallback (us-west request routed to eu pool) added ~220ms extra median due to network. So prefer local SXM pools for low-latency SLAs, and use model-fallback policy for cost tiering.

raj: any surprises about kernel selection interactions with quantization?

maya: yes — our custom fused kernel needed slight tweaks for int8 (accumulator width and reorder). Without those we saw correctness issues on longer seqs (>2048), fixed by forcing int32 accumulation in the reduce path.

sasha: action items?

maya: 1) add NUMA pinning to the default SXM node startup scripts (oliver flagged). 2) bake CUSTOM_KV_PULL for SXM-only deployment and keep CUTLASS for PCIe. 3) create canary rollout with eval hooks for int8.

oliver: I can add numactl snippet to node-provisioning, will open infra PR.

raj: i'll schedule longer stress runs (24h) on both topologies to validate stability and memory growth.

maya: thanks. I'll upload full perf logs + flamegraphs to the internal bucket: s3://redwood-bench/topo-smoke/1781249876/. ping if you want the raw perf counters.

bench-bot: benchmark run 1781249876 finished: artifacts uploaded. :white_check_mark:

maya: cc @sasha @raj @oliver — follow-ups in the PRs. short thread, happy to walk through numbers in 15m if helpful. :thumbsup:
